title: Onset of the transitional flux-avalanche regime in bulk NbTi controlled by the thermal boundary conductance
authors: Irina Abaloszewa, Victor V. Chabanenko, Aleksander Abaloszew
abstract: Thermomagnetic avalanches in type-II superconductors occur in two qualitatively different regimes, electromagnetically controlled in thin films and thermally limited in bulk samples, distinguished by the sign of the temperature derivative of the threshold field $H_\text{th}(T)$. The two regimes are separated by a critical thermal boundary conductance $h_c$, and a non-monotonic $H_\text{th}(T)$ has been predicted in the transitional region where the interface conductance $h$ approaches $h_c$. We approach this region in a bulk NbTi disk by raising the interface coupling above the pure-nonadecane baseline with a silver-filled interface layer. Whereas the pure interface gives a monotonically decreasing $H_\text{th}(T)$, the silver-filled interface produces a non-monotonic dependence not previously realized in a bulk superconductor: a temperature interval of positive slope, $dH_\text{th}/dT > 0$, terminating in a maximum at $T^* \approx 6.1$--$6.4$~K. The effect is reproduced for two independent silver-filled compositions; in a third, with the highest loading, the low-temperature decrease is absent altogether and $H_\text{th}(T)$ is flat up to the same $T^*$, the evolution expected for stronger coupling. The position of the maximum is set by the intrinsic properties of NbTi, independent of the silver content. The onset of the positive-slope interval coincides in temperature with a change of the avalanche morphology from narrow channeled fingers to broad fronts. The reversal of the sign of $dH_\text{th}/dT$ is a direct experimental signature of the onset of the transitional regime, in which heat removal during the instability becomes dynamically relevant.
summary: This work experimentally investigates how modifying the thermal interface conductance in bulk NbTi superconductors alters the temperature dependence of flux avalanches. By introducing silver into the sample interface, the researchers induced a unique non-monotonic behavior in the threshold field $H_{th}(T)$. This signature is identified as direct evidence for entering a transitional regime where dynamic heat removal plays a crucial role.
main_problem: The study investigates the onset of a transitional flux-avalanche regime in bulk Type-II superconductors, determining how thermal boundary conductance controls the superconducting instability.
main_result: Incorporating silver into the thermal interface layer causes the threshold field $H_{th}(T)$ to exhibit non-monotonic behavior, including an interval where $	ext{dH}_{th}/	ext{dT} > 0$, which signals entry into this transitional regime.
method: Measurements were performed using magneto-optical imaging (MOI) on bulk NbTi disks with interfaces modified by varying concentrations of silver powder.
model_or_system: The physical system is a bulk Type-II superconductor (NbTi) undergoing thermomagnetic avalanches. The key control parameter is the thermal boundary conductance ($h$) at the sample interface, which dictates the transition between electromagnetically and thermally controlled regimes.
key_observables: $H_{th}(T)$ (threshold field vs. temperature), $	ext{dH}_{th}/	ext{dT}$ (slope of $H_{th}$), and avalanche morphology (fingers vs. fronts).
important_parameters: Critical thermal boundary conductance ($h_c$), silver loading concentration ($	ext{wt.}\%$ Ag), and the characteristic temperature $T^* \approx 6.1-6.4$ K.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed non-monotonicity is a direct experimental signature of dynamic heat removal becoming relevant during the instability process, distinguishing it from purely quasi-static predictions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows $H_{th}(T)$ for various Ag concentrations, highlighting the positive slope region ($	ext{dH}_{th}/	ext{dT} > 0$) in silver-filled interfaces. Figure 2 relates this to avalanche morphology changes (fingers to fronts).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the background of flux avalanche regimes, details the experimental modification using Ag-filled interfaces, presents the key results showing non-monotonic $H_{th}(T)$ behavior, and correlates this change with both the transition into the transitional regime and changes in avalanche morphology.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the core concept of identifying a critical parameter ($h_c$) that dictates a qualitative phase/regime crossover based on thermal coupling is highly relevant to open quantum systems where environmental coupling drives non-equilibrium dynamics.
